title: Telemedical Anamnesis and Risk Assessment
summary: Before surgery, patients usually travel to hospital for an anaesthetic consultation, which can be inconvenient and time-consuming. The TARA study tests whether the same counselling can be delivered safely and effectively via a secure video call. At University Hospital Aachen, two sequential cohorts will be compared: first 250 adults receiving the standard on-site visit, then 250 adults counseled from home by video. Immediately after the consultation, questionnaires assess how well prepared and satisfied patients feel and whether they understand and follow pre-operative instructions. The study also records staff workload, consultation time and any adverse events. Findings will reveal whether video-based counselling is a convenient, equivalent alternative to an in-person visit to the pre-anaesthesia clinic.
conditions: Pre-operative anaesthesia evaluation / peri-operative risk assessment
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scheduled for elective surgery requiring anaesthetic care; Able to give informed consent; Access to an internet-enabled device with camera and microphone
Exclusion criteria:
Language or cognitive barriers (e.g. profound language barrier, dementia, history of laryngectomy resulting in loss of voice); High surgical risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiac-related death within 30 days post-operation according to the criteria described by Halvorsen et al.; Emergency procedures
